svg.title: EL34 output tube — internal structure
svg.desc: The EL34 power pentode: cathode at the center heated by a filament, surrounded by control grid g1, screen grid g2, suppressor grid g3, and an outer plate. Eight-pin octal base.
svg.text: Power pentode: three grids between the cathode and the plate. Indirectly heated.

g.title:
PLATE (anode) — pin 3.
The outer envelope of the electron-collecting structure. Receives B+ (~450 V DC) through the output transformer primary (step 8). Audio signal swings ride on top of this DC.
In normal operation, electrons emitted by the heated cathode are pulled across the vacuum to the plate. The grids in between control how many get through.

SUPPRESSOR GRID (g3) — internally tied to cathode in the EL34.
Sits between the plate and the screen grid. Its job: catch secondary electrons knocked out of the plate so they don't end up on the screen grid (which would mess up the pentode's characteristic curve at low plate voltages).
In the EL34 specifically, g3 is internally connected to the cathode — so there's no external pin for it. You see this in the pin list: pins 1, 6 are internal connections.

SCREEN GRID (g2) — pin 4.
Held at ~400 V DC (slightly below B+ via a series dropping resistor). Accelerates electrons from the cathode toward the plate AND shields the control grid from plate voltage swings.
The "ultralinear" tap on the A-470 output transformer connects g2 to a fractional point on the primary, giving a hybrid of pentode and triode characteristics. The ST-70 runs UL by default — that's the GREEN lead on the OPT.

CONTROL GRID (g1) — pin 5.
The audio input. Held at ~−36 to −40 V DC by the bias supply (step 1 → 1N4007 → bias pots) and "modulated" up and down by the audio signal from the driver stage.
A small voltage swing on g1 produces a large current swing through the plate — this is what amplification IS.
If g1 drifts too positive (bias supply fails / hot bias), the tube draws runaway current and red-plates. If g1 drifts too negative, the tube cuts off and distorts.

CATHODE (sleeve) — pin 8.
Heated indirectly by the filament inside. Emits electrons that the grids modulate and the plate collects.
In the ST-70, the cathode is grounded through a small (1 Ω) "cathode resistor" — measuring the DC voltage across that resistor with Ohm's law gives you the tube's idle current (used during bias-up).

HEATER FILAMENT — 6.3 V AC @ 1.5 A.
Inside the cathode sleeve, heating it indirectly. The two heater leads land at pins 2 and 7. In the ST-70 these are chained to the corresponding pins on V3 / V6 / V7 (and on to the 6GH8A driver tubes) — see step 4 for the start of that chain.

svg.text: Octal base — pin numbering as viewed from the wiring side (below the chassis)

g.title:
Pin 1 — Internal connection.
On many EL34s this is internally tied to the suppressor (g3) and to the cathode. Often left disconnected externally, sometimes used as a chassis-shield tie. Check the datasheet for your specific tube.

Pin 2 — Heater.
One end of the 6.3 V heater filament. The GRN/BRN lead from the PA-060 lands here in step 4 (or step 5 for V7), with chain jumpers to V3 / V6 / driver tubes on later pages.

Pin 3 — Plate (anode).
Receives B+ via the output transformer primary (step 8). Audio signal swings ride on top of the ~450 V DC.

Pin 4 — Screen grid (g2).
Fed from B+ through a series dropping resistor (or the OPT's UL tap if running ultralinear, which the ST-70 does by default). ~400 V DC nominal.

Pin 5 — Control grid (g1).
The audio input. Sees the driver-stage output coupled through a coupling cap, plus the bias DC voltage (~−40 V) from the bias supply chain (step 1 → 1N4007 → bias pots).

Pin 6 — Internal connection.
Usually unused externally; on some EL34s it's another shield/g3 tie. Treat as NC unless your specific tube's datasheet says otherwise.

Pin 7 — Heater (other end).
Other end of the 6.3 V heater filament; the second lead in each heater pair lands here.

Pin 8 — Cathode.
In the ST-70, cathode connects to a small (1 Ω) sense resistor to ground. Measuring DC volts across that resistor gives the idle current via Ohm's law — that's how bias is set during bring-up.

svg.text: Indirectly heated · 6.3 V × 1.5 A heater · ~450 V plate · ~400 V screen · ~−40 V grid bias · cathode at ~0 V (with 1 Ω sense resistor)
